analysis:
Only scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py changed: a unit test that pins release-pipeline properties. It ships no runtime code, and the file is not in the provider process, WebSocket contract or App Attest paths. I saw three changed regions (base 368-369, 695-698, 854-856; head 368-372, 698-701, 857-859). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the last hunk is only partly visible.

(1) test_warming_cannot_publish_or_seed_default_branch_from_pr (base 367-383). It now expects a nightly cron trigger in provider-cache-warming, no push-to-master branch trigger, no 'scripts/**' path filter, and cancel-in-progress. It also expects the warm job to be gated on needs.gate.outputs.run. The test still forbids secrets, contents: write, gh release create, aws s3 and notarytool in WARM and ACTION, and still forbids pull_request_target and workflow_run. The warm cache therefore stays unable to publish or use secrets. The workflow edits are not in this batch, so I cannot confirm the gate job, the schedule or the removed push trigger. Cache poisoning is a possible concern: a PR-warmed cache could affect release builds. The existing assertion that PR warming uses a different runner and a different cache scope is unchanged.

(2) test_the_cluster_runtime_scripts_start_the_release_lanes (base 693-698). The release-dev-branch.yml assertion is loosened from a literal '      - script' line to a substring match of the quoted script name. That is a weaker pin but still checks the script is listed. The dev caller's trigger structure may have changed; the workflow itself is not supplied.

(3) The publication-requirements path assertion near base 854-856 is truncated in the excerpt. It likely gets the same loosening for the dev caller.

No security assertions were removed in the visible regions. The signing, keychain, notarization-credential, secret-scoping, environment-gating and publish-permission tests are untouched. No finding qualifies. Residual question for integration: confirm the companion workflow changes in provider-cache-warming.yml and release-dev-branch.yml (not supplied) still satisfy the pinned invariants (no secrets, no write permissions, PR cache isolation), and that the weakened trigger-path checks do not hide a dropped release trigger.
